  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Fact: deliver a small Python HTTP service in which organisers create events with seat counts and people reserve seats; its usable target is the service’s HTTP interface, and the request grants delivery there but does not name a deployment target. Fact: the repository is empty, this unattended run covers intake only, and implementation is outside this stage. Assumption: use an unauthenticated interface with shared, in-memory event and reservation counts for callers of one running process; state lasts until that process ends, does not persist across restarts or span processes, and identifies no individual person. Assumption: reservations cannot exceed capacity, including concurrent requests; no event or reservation data is assumed private, and only exposed API responses are visible to callers. These defaults rule out durable storage, cross-process coordination, individual attribution, and access-controlled visibility unless discovery finds a requirement for them. Open item — discovery: establish the available Python runtime and execution environment first, then determine the HTTP contract, any existing identity or state facilities, privacy expectations, reservation semantics, and persistence needs; these findings block final implementation choices. Source hints, not verified facts: the request’s terms ‘organisers’, ‘people’, and ‘reserve seats’, plus any later-available workspace documentation, runtime configuration, or service owner; no team, channel, internal site, private repository, or owner was named. Risk: concurrent reservations and process restarts affect capacity and state. Fact: an isolated source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; a deployed outcome would be visible only after release, and no release target is specified. S2 — Fact: include tests for the service; the tests and their results become usable in the delivered source checkout at final return, with test tooling and commands to be determined after discovery establishes the runtime."
}
